query: For a high-entropy alloy initially designed as a single-phase solid solution, what testable mechanistic hypothesis explains whether and why it loses toughness or undergoes brittle fracture under mechanical loading in demanding engineering service? Define a controlled comparison that would reveal the governing behavior, predict observations relative to the initial baseline, identify the applicable service and loading boundaries, cite supporting prior evidence, and state a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: High-temperature service exposure induces precipitation of brittle B2-ordered intermetallic phases at grain boundaries in an initially single-phase fcc high-entropy alloy, leading to stress‐concentrated intergranular cracking and a measurable loss of fracture toughness under mechanical loading.
generation.material_initial_state: As-annealed single-phase fcc CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy, average grain size ~20 µm, no detectable second phases.
generation.intervention: Thermal aging at 600 °C for 100 h in inert atmosphere.
generation.conditions: Quasi-static fracture toughness tests at room temperature, strain rate ≈1×10⁻⁴ s⁻¹; service boundary: exposure temperatures ≥ 500 °C and stress intensity factors ≥ 50 MPa·√m.
generation.structural_mediator: Nanometer-scale B2-ordered precipitates at grain boundaries and subgrain interfaces.
generation.mechanism: Brittle precipitates act as crack‐nucleation sites under stress, promoting intergranular crack propagation and reducing energy dissipation during fracture.
generation.predicted_outcome: Aged specimens will exhibit a ≈30% reduction in K_IC relative to the as-annealed baseline and fracture surfaces dominated by intergranular features and cleavage facets.
generation.boundary: No significant embrittlement if aging temperature < 500 °C or duration < 10 h; embrittlement observed for stress intensity factors ≥ 50 MPa·√m.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate—precipitation kinetics and exact toughness reduction magnitude may vary with minor composition shifts.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of CoCrFeMnNi specimens: (1) as-annealed, (2) aged at 600 °C for 100 h. Characterize precipitate formation via transmission electron microscopy (TEM). Measure fracture toughness (K_IC) using ASTM E399. Examine fracture surfaces with scanning electron microscopy (SEM).
measurements: TEM identification and size distribution of B2 precipitates
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If aged specimens show no significant decrease in K_IC beyond ±5% scatter and TEM detects no B2 precipitates at grain boundaries, then the hypothesis is falsified.
